# Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta (SN 49)

**ID:** SN 49  
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul4.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0305m.mul4.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 49), translated as "Linked Discourses on the Right Efforts" or "Connected Discourses on the Right Strivings", is the forty-ninth section of the *Saṁyuttanikāya* and forms the fifth chapter of its concluding *Mahāvagga* [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. It represents one of the seven saṁyuttas in the *Mahāvagga* devoted to the fundamental sets of training factors that constitute the Buddhist path to awakening (*bodhipakkhiyā dhammā*) [Bodhi 2003; Gethin 2008].

The collection contains 54 discourses arranged into five vaggas, beginning with the *Gaṅgāpeyyālavagga* and *Appamādavagga* [Hazra 1994]. Rather than assembling unique or freestanding suttas, the saṁyutta is structured as a systematic instantiation of the standard repetition series (*peyyāla*) framed around the canonical stock formula of the four right strivings (*cattāro sammappadhānā*) [Bodhi 2003]. This formula defines the monk's arousal of desire, effort, energy, and mental striving toward four ends: preventing the arising of unarisen evil unwholesome states, abandoning arisen unwholesome states, arousing unarisen wholesome states, and maintaining and perfecting arisen wholesome states [Bodhi 2003; Hazra 1994]. Although numerous discourses treating right effort appear scattered throughout the wider Pali Nikāyas, canonical redactors chose not to collect them here, restricting the saṁyutta to this repetitive schematic treatment.

Parallels to portions of the collection survive in the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99), notably SĀ 875–878 for the *Gaṅgāpeyyālavagga* (SN 49.1–12) and SĀ 882 for the *Appamādavagga* (SN 49.13–22).

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A Translation of the Samyutta Nikaya (2003) — Provided English title, chapter placement in the Mahāvagga, analysis of the repetition series structure, and the stock formula of the four right strivings.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Provided description of the five chapters and doctrinal enumeration of the four right strivings.
- [Gethin 2008] Rupert Gethin, Sayings of the Buddha: New Translations from the Pali Nikayas (2008) — Confirmed the placement and thematic role of the Sammappadhāna Saṁyutta within the Mahāvagga's seven core groups.
